sentences.text: Yuanjiawaornis is classified as an extinct genus of large enantiornithean bird, a group of early avians.
The femur of the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — measures forty-three millimetres in length.
Its wings and hindlimbs were roughly the same length, suggesting a balanced build for movement.
The lower leg formed a fused tibiotarsus over five centimetres long, a structure common in birds.
The first toe claw was robust and strongly curved, directed backwards, likely aiding in perching or grasping.
The specific name 'viriosus' means 'powerful' in Latin, referring to the bird's large body size.
The unfused hand in the holotype suggests the specimen was a young adult, offering a glimpse into its growth stage.
The fossil was excavated in 2005 by a museum team in Liaoning and formally named in 2015.
The species was described by Hu Dongyu, Liu Ying, Li Jinhua, Xu Xing, and Hou Lianhai.
Researchers placed the bird within Enantiornithes based on typical features like a Y-shaped wishbone and specific rib facets.
The animal lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now China.
The fossil dates to the Aptian stage, approximately 120 million years ago.
The time range for the genus is estimated between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
The exact phylogenetic relationships of Yuanjiawaornis remain uncertain because the skull has not been found.
